dp.name: Default Policies
dp.title: Default Policies
dp.lede: These are your office defaults: what a new project starts with and what new things get. A project you already started is not changed.
dp.app.hint: A policy left on "{app}'s own" changes nothing: {app} then does what it always did. The office name and the policies for every app are in Settings › Global › Default Policies.
dp.saved: Saved. New projects start this way.
dp.saved.unset: Saved. This is {app}'s own default again.
dp.err.range: That is outside what this policy allows ({min} to {max}).
dp.err.type: That is not a value this policy can take.
dp.err.empty: Type a value, or clear the box to go back to the app's own default.
dp.err.option: That choice is not offered here.
dp.err.value: That value could not be saved.
dp.err.length: Type a length, for example 3000 mm or 10'-0".
dp.group.audit: Audit: the LOD each project stage asks for
dp.office.placeholder: For example: Smith and Jones Architects
dp.office.hint: Optional. It is written into the file you save, so people can tell whose defaults they are.
dp.count.none: No policy is set: every app uses its own defaults.
dp.file.hint: Save the policies as a small open file (JSON) to share across the office; loading a file replaces the policies on this computer.
dp.file.export.title: Save every policy on this computer as one file to share
dp.file.import.title: Replace the policies on this computer with a file's
dp.file.ignored: Left out {n} that this version does not know or cannot use: {list}.
dp.file.newer: The file was written by a later version.
dp.file.err.read: That file could not be read.
dp.file.err.json: That file is not a Default Policies file (it is not JSON).
dp.file.err.format: That file is not a Default Policies file.
dp.file.err.size: That file is too large to be a Default Policies file.
dp.file.err.save: The file could not be saved.
dp.reset.all.title: Every app goes back to its own defaults
dp.reset.all.done: Every policy is reset: every app uses its own defaults.
dp.reset.app.done: {app}'s policies are reset: it uses its own defaults.
dp.p.all.system: Unit system of a new project
dp.p.all.system.hint: For every app. An app's own units policy, when set, comes first.
dp.p.all.anno.text.hint: Millimetres on the printed sheet (the height of a capital letter). The model is drawn full size; a new building takes these heights and keeps them at every drawing scale.
dp.p.all.anno.title: View titles on sheets
dp.p.all.schedule.group.hint: Used by every schedule that has such a column and does not state its own grouping.
dp.o.all.schedule.totals.groups: A subtotal under each group and a total
dp.p.all.schedule.title: Schedule title
dp.o.all.schedule.headings.title: With Capitals
dp.p.bimcraft.units.hint: The units switch to this when a new building is created. BimCraft has no precision setting, so there is none here.
dp.p.bimcraft.levels.name: Level names
dp.p.bimcraft.wall.first.hint: What the Wall tool draws first in a new building.
dp.p.bimcraft.wall.starterLod: LOD tag on the starter wall types
dp.p.bimcraft.wall.starterLod.hint: Shown wherever a starter type is listed, on this computer. A type made as a copy of a starter keeps the tag in the file.
dp.p.bimcraft.wall.newLod: LOD of a newly made wall type
dp.p.bimcraft.audit.lod.concept.hint: The audit reports elements below this level of development at that stage. CadCraft's own starting values are not a standard: set your project's.
dp.o.bimcraft.sheet.first.sheet: A first sheet with the lowest level's plan
dp.p.bimcraft.sheet.title: Sheet name
dp.p.bimcraft.tool.afterCreate: Tool that is active after Create
dp.p.cadcraft.length.precision.hint: Decimal places, 0 to 8. For architectural and fractional lengths it is the power of two of the smallest fraction (4 = 1/16).
